items.title: Samsung’s Auto Blocker won’t switch off during calls in One UI 9.5
items.summary:
Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

With One UI 9.5, users won’t be able to change Auto Blocker settings during a call. 
 This is to thwart scammers trying to get people to disable security features. 
 The feature is already live in the first One UI 9.5 beta on the Galaxy S26. 

Samsung’s One UI comes with Auto Blocker , which warns you before sideloading APKs and protects your Galaxy phone or tablet from malicious execution over USB or from harmful files received via messaging apps. With One UI 9.5 beta that rolled out to the Galaxy S26 series earlier this week, Auto Blocker appears to be getting additional anti-scam features that prevent hackers from misguiding users during calls.

Since Auto Blocker prevents unauthorized apps from being installed, scammers may often attempt to lure users into changing security settings on their devices. Getting users to change these settings makes it easier for scammers to install malicious apps and take over these devices. To prevent this, Samsung is raising the threshold for Auto Blocker and adding measures that prevent users from changing crucial settings while they’re on calls.
items.t: Samsung’s Auto Blocker won’t switch off during calls in One UI 9.5

items.title: GrapheneOS claims Google is now waging war against it, could lock Pixel bootloader
items.summary:
Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

The GrapheneOS team has claimed that Google was trying to harm the project and wipe it out. 
 Google was allegedly contacting Android OEMs to ask whether they were working with GrapheneOS, and was purportedly threatening these brands. 
 The team also suggested that Google could start locking the bootloader on Pixels and taking other actions to make Android forks unviable. 

GrapheneOS is the leading Android fork if you want a secure and private smartphone experience. Pixels were the only officially supported platform, but the team is also working with Motorola to launch a Motorola Signature 27 phone with GrapheneOS . However, the developers of this software have now made some interesting claims against Google.

The GrapheneOS team claimed on X that Google was contacting Android OEMs to ask whether them whether they were working with the GrapheneOS project. Furthermore, the team asserts that Google was threatening these brands by citing Google Mobile Services licensing terms.

 Users will need an Android OS update, not a Google Play System update, to get Google’s current implementation of App Lock. 

Between Samsung introducing native app lock in One UI 9.5 this week and Google restoring the feature in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 last month, it’s been a good few weeks for Android users who value their privacy. items.title: Gemini could soon make it easy to find chats where you left unfinished draft text
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is working on indicators to show when you’ve left a draft message in Gemini chats. 
 Users would be able to filter the chat list to only show those with active drafts. 
 Gemini’s also working on new tools for sharing chat output and Live prompts. 

Working with an AI as powerful as Gemini can be a little overwhelming — where do you even start, with so many options available to you — and if you frequently find yourself leaving things hanging before you finish sharing your latest thoughts with Gemini, you just might appreciate what looks like a new feature for managing your drafts. We’ve uncovered evidence for just that, as well as new tools for sharing your Gemini sessions, in a recent app update.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Gemini already saves drafts that you’ve started writing but have yet to submit. The problem right now is that there’s no good way to find them. If you pull up your list of past chats, when you tap on one you’ll see any draft text still in the box, but there’s no way to know that’s there from your main list of chats in the app’s menu.

items.title: Google brings computer use to Mac, letting Gemini handle chores without hijacking your screen
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is rolling out computer use to the Gemini app for Mac, allowing it to operate desktop apps and websites on your behalf. 
 Gemini works in an isolated background window, leaving your screen and cursor free while you monitor its progress in real time. 
 The feature requires an Apple Silicon Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription, and is initially available in the US. 

When Google brought Gemini Spark to the Mac earlier this year, it gave its AI assistant access to local files, allowing it to handle chores like organizing folders and turning documents into spreadsheets. But working with files on your computer and actually operating the apps installed on it are two different things. Google’s latest Gemini update bridges that gap.

Just two days after making Gemini Tasks available for free and adding the ability to call businesses, make purchases, and accept requests via text and email, Google is rolling out computer use to the Gemini app for Mac . The feature, which we first learned was in testing in September , lets Gemini click buttons, type, navigate menus, and fill out forms across desktop apps and websites on your behalf.
items.t: Google brings computer use to Mac, letting Gemini handle chores without hijacking your screen

items.title: Fitbit Edge owners are complaining about the lack of hourly movement reminders
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Fitbit Edge owners report that the tracker lacks hourly reminders to move. 
 The tracker still monitors hourly activity but doesn’t vibrate to remind users to reach their 250-step goal. 
 Reminders to move have been available on Fitbit devices since 2016, helping users stay active throughout the day. 

One of the simplest ways Fitbit has helped people stay active over the years is by encouraging them to get out of their chairs. As far back as the original Fitbit Alta in 2016, Fitbit offered reminders to move. Rather than letting you cram all your daily steps into an evening walk, the feature encouraged you to spread your activity throughout the day. However, those upgrading to the new Google Fitbit Edge are discovering that their wrists have gone unusually quiet.

Reports on Reddit , Facebook ( 2 ), and the Google Health Community reveal that the Fitbit Edge lacks an option to enable hourly reminders to move. While the tracker still records hourly activity, it apparently doesn’t vibrate to remind you when you’re falling short of your 250-step hourly goal.
items.t: Fitbit Edge owners are complaining about the lack of hourly movement reminders

items.title: Samsung prepares Galaxy AI on Snapdragon X Elite for its upcoming Android laptops
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals that Samsung is preparing on-device Galaxy AI features for its upcoming Snapdragon X Elite-powered Android laptops, codenamed Origin. 
 Samsung AI Core adds local support for Generative Edit, in-painting and out-painting, and harmonization, while Samsung Semantic Core lists the chip for on-device Gauss language, translation, and vision models. 
 Samsung Video Editor adds a Snapdragon X Elite X1E-80-100 profile with flagship 8K editing limits, alongside new references in Samsung Gallery, and Samsung Device Health Manager. 

Samsung is getting Galaxy AI ready for the Snapdragon X Elite, the chip inside its upcoming Android laptops. Samsung’s on-device AI apps on the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 now list the chip, which we’ve tied to Samsung’s laptops codenamed Origin . The same build also reveals the laptops’ dedicated One UI interface with Circle to Search and how they’ll plug into the Galaxy ecosystem .

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung already sells Windows laptops with the Snapdragon X Elite, like the Galaxy Book4 Edge, and they offer some Galaxy AI features through Windows apps. The new entries in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 are different: they sit in the Android versions of Samsung’s AI apps, so they’re meant for One UI running on the laptop itself.
items.t: Samsung prepares Galaxy AI on Snapdragon X Elite for its upcoming Android laptops

items.title: Samsung could bring native Open Gate video recording and dual-cam panorama to its smartphones with One UI 9.5
items.summary:
Samsung announced the One UI 9.5 beta program for the Galaxy S26 series yesterday. One UI 9.5 brings several new features, including App Lock and Floating shortcuts. With future One UI 9.5 updates, Samsung could bring more features to Galaxy smartphones, including native Open Gate video recording and dual-cam panorama.

This revelation comes from Android Authority, which found strings related to native Open Gate video recording and dual-cam panorama in One UI 9.5's Camera app code.
